newsitem.title: CHINA: China finds state assets 74 pct of end-94 amount.
newsitem.headline: China finds state assets 74 pct of end-94 amount.

text.p: China has completed its annual assessment of state assets for 1995 and found their account value was down to 74 percent of the total at the end of 1994, the Xinhua news agency said on Friday.

A total of 83,315 large and medium-sized state-owned enterprises had been examined by the end of July, including 4,326 companies run by the central authorities, and 78,989 local firms, said the assessment by the State Administration of State Property.

The initial analysis showed the account value of state-owned rights and interests of the assessed enterprises was 74 percent of the total amount of all state-owned enterprises at the end of the previous year, it said.
The value of state-owned assets in the examined enterprises grew by 3.59 percent in 1995, 0.59 percent higher than the target set at the beginning of last year.

The analysis showed that 84 percent of the added value was reported in enterprises run by the central authorities, and the value of state property appreciated most in the automobile, post and telecommunications, tobacco, petrochemicals, power and petroleum sectors.
It showed that coastal areas and new industrial centres outperformed the interior areas and old industrial bases in maintaining and increasing the value of state property.

An administration official said the overall operation of state-owned property was not satisfactory, because the 3.59 percent growth rate for the value of state property was far lower than the interest rates on bank deposits for the same period.
A high asset-to-liability ratio and a high ratio of bad assets were two major elements behind the poor performance of state property, the official said.
Other factors included a lack of liquidity of available assets, disorder in the management of investments and inadequate measures to reduce losses, he said.
